Industry News: Lumentum CEO defends Marvell deal after stock plunge: 'We've got work to do' with shareholders

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (630 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston defended the tech giant's planned merger with chipmaker Marvell Technology on Thursday, acknowledging that the deal has received a disappointing reception.
  • Our numbers are phenomenal, and we feel the combination is even more powerful," Hurlston told CNBC's Jim Cramer on "Mad Money." Nevertheless, Hurlston said, "Shareholders are not happy ...
  • Shares of Marvell and Lumentum have tumbled 45% and 42%, respectively, since the close on Oct.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston defended the tech giant's planned merger with chipmaker Marvell Technology on Thursday, acknowledging that the deal has received a disappointing reception.

"Their numbers are phenomenal. Our numbers are phenomenal, and we feel the combination is even more powerful," Hurlston told CNBC's Jim Cramer on "Mad Money." Nevertheless, Hurlston said, "Shareholders are not happy ... It's been a tough couple of weeks.".

Shares of Marvell and Lumentum have tumbled 45% and 42%, respectively, since the close on Oct. 28. That night, Bloomberg News reported Marvell was nearing a megadeal to buy Lumentum, sending shockwaves through the market and beginning the wild ride that both stocks have been on. The tie-up was officially declared on the morning of Nov. 2 with the deal expected to close in the first half of 2028. At the time, the all-stock deal implied an enterprise value of $115 billion for Lumentum.

Beginning on Oct. 29, Marvell shares experienced three straight days of double-digit percentage declines. In total, they've advanced in just three sessions since the Oct. 28 close. For its part, Lumentum rose modestly on Oct. 29 following the initial M&A rumor. Then the selling pressure arrived, as investors questioned the merits of the deal. The stock has been green in five sessions since the Bloomberg report.

Recent findings suggest that the merger would combine Marvell's semiconductor and networking technology with Lumentum's optical components as AI data centers increasingly shift from copper wiring to fiber-optic connections to handle faster data transmission. Hurlston said that transition, rather than simply the construction of more data centers, will be a major growth driver for the planned combined entity.

In a recent development, "We've got work to do with our shareholders," Hurlston said, though he sees catalysts on the horizon that could help change their minds. He pointed to Marvell's earnings report scheduled for Dec. 1 and the upcoming release of a securities filing, known as an S-4, required as part of the merger process.

It has been revealed that "As people see [Marvell CEO Matt Murphy's] earnings he's going to announce in early December, we've got the S-4 coming out that's going to describe how both businesses are performing, we've got our earnings … I think those things together will give the shareholders confidence that, look, there's nothing wrong here. I mean, these businesses are great, and they're even better together," said Hurlston, who has led Lumentum since February 2025.

To be sure, the dramatic decline in both Marvell and Lumentum shares isn't entirely due to the investor displeasure with the planned transaction. In recent weeks, the market has soured on the AI trade more broadly, amid questions about the sustainability of the AI buildout due to higher borrowing costs and political backlash on data center construction, which was exemplified by the midterm election results. Though Hurlston acknowledged these other forces affecting the stocks and leading to compressed valuation multiples, he emphasized the work that he needs to do to win shareholder support.

Despite concerns about the broader AI buildout, Hurlston remarked Lumentum has seen no slowdown in demand. The company reported better-than-expected quarterly results on the day the merger was unveiled, with revenue more than doubling from a year earlier.

"I think we're going to get that multiple back once we can show our numbers and show how strong the two businesses are doing," he said.

    Breaking: U.K.-India trade deal faces a stiff test over Scotch whisky import taxes

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (723 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that within months of taking effect, the India-U.K.
    • Industry observers note that duty on bulk Scotch whisky imports was expected to be slashed to 75% then gradually to 40% over 10 years as per the trade agreement.
    • While India's commerce ministry did not respond to CNBC's request for comments, experts mentioned that authorities in India classify bulk Scotch as a raw material and claim the preferential tariffs accorded in the deal apply only to imported bottled Scotch.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that within months of taking effect, the India-U.K. trade deal is facing an early test, as Latest Delhi resists extending preferential tariffs to bulk Scotch whisky imports.

    Industry observers note that duty on bulk Scotch whisky imports was expected to be slashed to 75% then gradually to 40% over 10 years as per the trade agreement. However, a Reuters report Thursday mentioned that India now intends to levy a 162.5% duty on these imports, higher than the 150% in place before the trade deal.

    While India's commerce ministry did not respond to CNBC's request for comments, experts mentioned that authorities in India classify bulk Scotch as a raw material and claim the preferential tariffs accorded in the deal apply only to imported bottled Scotch.

    Amid the confusion over tax rates, thousands of liters of bulk Scotch in more than 80 shipping containers belonging to Pernod, Diageo and Bacardi are stuck at Indian ports, according to Reuters.

    Industry observers note that "Ministers are urgently working with the Government of India to resolve this issue to ensure UK businesses can export under the tariffs agreed in the trade deal," a U.K. government spokesperson told CNBC.

    Distillers in India use bulk Scotch in their own locally blended whisky brands. As a result, Indian tax authorities are classifying bulk Scotch as "compound alcoholic preparations" which do not qualify for the preferential rate, said Sohrab Bararia, partner and leader of global trade at Grant Thornton Bharat.

    Meanwhile, distillers argue that "genuine Scotch whisky" does not cease to be whisky merely because it is imported in bulk containers or used later for blending and bottling in India, Bararia remarked.

    Sources indicate that after three years, including 14 rounds of rigorous negotiations, India and the U.K. finalized the deal last year, which is expected to boost bilateral trade by 25.5 billion pounds ($34 billion) per year by 2040.

    Officials from Diageo and Chivas Brothers had cheered the trade deal and underscored its importance for Scotch and Scotland.

    "India is the world's largest whisky market by volume, so Scotch was always going to be one of the biggest prizes for the UK in this deal," said Reema Bhattacharya, head of Asia research at risk intelligence manufacturer Verisk Maplecroft.

    Instead of simply exporting bottled whisky, bulk scotch exports offer British producers long-term ties with companies in India, deepening their stake in the South Asian country's domestic alcoholic beverage industry, Bhattacharya noted.

    In the global spirits markets, while the U.S., Europe, and China are facing volume contraction, ageing populations, and shifting social habits, nearly 100 million new consumers will be of legal drinking age in India over the next five years, Indian brokerage HDFC Institutional Research remarked in a report in September.

    Sources indicate that the alcoholic beverage market in India is dominated by Indian-made foreign liquors (IMFL), as per the report. IMFL refers to alcoholic beverages produced in India by combining local spirits often with imported malts and flavorings.

    Greater access to bulk Scotch stocks at competitive prices helps Indian distilleries to improve blending quality for premium whisky products while maintaining cost efficiency, experts said. However, the latest dispute poses a major threat to these operations.

    Industry observers note that the lack of preferential tariffs on bulk Scotch could have "substantial" financial implications for importers, Parth Shah, partner at Deloitte India, told CNBC. "This could particularly affect Indian manufacturers who have invested in domestic blending and bottling operations using imported bulk Scotch whisky," he added.

    Diageo-owned United Spirits, Pernod Ricard and Indian firms Allied Blenders and Radico Khaitan own and market some of the popular whisky brands in India.

    Companies and industry bodies, the International Spirits and Wine Association and Confederation of Indian Alcoholic Beverage Companies, did not respond to CNBC's requests for comment.

    A spokesperson for one of the whisky makers told CNBC that industry bodies were in talks with the commerce ministry to "represent adherence to the India-UK FTA." The person did not wish to be identified as they fear it could lead to a potential backlash from regulators.

    "The lesson for the EU and other partners negotiating with India is that securing a headline tariff reduction is only half the battle," Bhattacharya of Maplecroft Verisk said, adding that partners need to pay close attention to whether "concessions translate into actual market access.".

    #4048. What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (747 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (747 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the manufacturer's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.
    • Industry observers note that huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the company.
    • It has been revealed that nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the manufacturer's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.

    Industry observers note that huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the company. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.

    It has been revealed that nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.

    "Although we expect the tech giant to fulfill all of its previously revealed commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate new multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider remarked in a note Thursday.

    The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.

    Tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.

    On Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.717%, nearly 5% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

    Tech stocks slumped Friday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 1.2% as markets continued to digest the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Friday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt lingers.

    Industry observers note that it's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The manufacturer had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.

    Neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.

    In a recent development, coreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.79% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped more than 17% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.

    It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, said CreditSights analyst Andy Li.

    "We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he said.

    "However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.

    CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday, before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person.".

    According to recent reports, "There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my company every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he said in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us.".

    Sources indicate that bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any major changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.

    The real issue is just how much money the firm will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.

    "Major companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he said. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies.".

    — CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.

    #4047. ‘More than just a game’: How GTA VI’s blockbuster launch fuels a booming content economy

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (698 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    ‘More than just a game’: How GTA VI’s blockbuster launch fuels a booming content economy

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (698 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Grand Theft Auto VI has exploded out of the gate after a 13-year wait, drawing millions of buyers while fueling a parallel economy of livestreams, clips and other content built around people watching the game as much as playing it.
    • Sources indicate that GTA VI has delivered a blockbuster debut, with about 19.1 million copies sold — including preorders — by Thursday morning, representing roughly $1.84 billion in sales, according to Sensor Tower.
    • Take-Two Interactive, which owns the studio behind the game, has not yet disclosed a profit figure for the title.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Grand Theft Auto VI has exploded out of the gate after a 13-year wait, drawing millions of buyers while fueling a parallel economy of livestreams, clips and other content built around people watching the game as much as playing it.

    Sources indicate that GTA VI has delivered a blockbuster debut, with about 19.1 million copies sold — including preorders — by Thursday morning, representing roughly $1.84 billion in sales, according to Sensor Tower. The GTA franchise itself has sold more than 470 million units worldwide.

    Take-Two Interactive, which owns the studio behind the game, has not yet disclosed a profit figure for the title.

    Ross Gerber, president and CEO of Gerber Kawasaki Wealth & Investment Management, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia" that he sees further upside for Take-Two, which his firm holds in its portfolio.

    Sources indicate that "It's crazy good. I've never seen anything like it," Gerber noted, hailing the title as "more than just a game" and pointing to the franchise's potential to expand into film and television.

    But that launch is also spawning a second economy around the enormous global hype and demand for GTA VI content.

    Viewers watched 125.5 million hours of the title's content in its first 24 hours across platforms including Twitch, YouTube and Kick, according to Streams Charts.

    According to recent reports, youTube creator Darren "IShowSpeed" Watkins Jr. led streamers with 4.47 million hours viewed across YouTube and Twitch. Separately, Twitch tracker CastAccord recorded about two million hours watched over roughly 36 hours of streamer Kai Cenat's launch broadcast.

    Recent findings suggest that both creators had built anticipation with trailers for their own GTA VI coverage. As of Nov. 19, IShowSpeed's trailer had drawn 3.7 million YouTube views, while Cenat's had amassed 2.7 million.

    According to Forbes, IShowSpeed and Cenat are estimated to earn about $30 million and $8.5 million a year, respectively, from their broader creator businesses.

    Rockstar Games, the studio behind the franchise, has also moved to capitalize on the surge in viewer interest, partnering with YouTube on a 24-hour launch broadcast and introducing themed gifts that viewers could send during select streams.

    Outside creators and agencies are also trying to capture the surge in demand for Grand Theft Auto content.

    Agency Clipped & Shipped is offering a $10,000 prize pool to editors who can drive audiences to clips from Kai Cenat's streams, with qualifying submissions distributed across YouTube Shorts, TikTok, Instagram and X.

    A separate campaign offered $1 per 1,000 views for clips of streamer KreekCraft, with individual submissions eligible to earn up to $400.

    Those audiences could translate into thousands of dollars in creator revenue.

    Using AIR Media-Tech's U.S. YouTube Shorts benchmark, 1.5 million eligible engaged views could generate about $490, while 5.1 million would yield roughly $1,670.

    According to recent reports, the two Vice City Dispatch videos could generate about $3,840 based on higher benchmark rates for long-form content. The channels' actual earnings could not be independently verified.

    Moreover, the content economy is becoming increasingly automated.

    On X, consumers are pitching artificial intelligence-assisted clipping operations that scan livestreams for spikes in chat activity, automatically cut highlights and distribute them across multiple accounts.

    One user claimed an operation generated $21,000 overnight from 2.7 million views, equivalent to about $7.78 per 1,000 reported views.

    It has been revealed that the earnings claims could not be independently verified. X bases payouts on qualified impressions from Premium owners, which are not reflected in public view counts.

    And appetite for more content — and more revenue — may only be starting.

    Wedbush analyst Alicia Reese told CNBC that in-game purchases could generate "years of high-margin recurring revenue" for Take-Two, which she believes investors have yet to fully price in.

    She expects the console launch to be followed by a PC release and then an online multiplayer mode, mirroring the rollout of the previous title in the franchise.

    • The Portland Trail Blazers made the trek to Milwaukee last year to play the Bucks.
    • Fiserv Forum aired a video tribute to Lillard amid that November 2025 meeting, and the nine-time All-Star received a standing ovation after it played that night.
    • Recent findings suggest that thursday marked the 36-year-old guard's first time taking the court against Milwaukee since his injury and his two-season stint with the Bucks.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Portland Trail Blazers made the trek to Milwaukee last year to play the Bucks. Damian Lillard was present, even though he was sitting out the entire 2025-26 campaign — his first season back with the Trail Blazers — as he recovered from the Achilles tear he suffered while playing for the Bucks in their 2025 first-round playoff series.

    Fiserv Forum aired a video tribute to Lillard amid that November 2025 meeting, and the nine-time All-Star received a standing ovation after it played that night.

    Recent findings suggest that thursday marked the 36-year-old guard's first time taking the court against Milwaukee since his injury and his two-season stint with the Bucks. Lillard was subdued talking about the matchup in the lead-up to tip-off, but he came away with his best performance in 624 days.

    In a recent development, march 5, 2025, was the last time Lillard had a 30-point game. He scored a season-high 33 points on Thursday in a 124-114 victory over a reeling and rebuilding Milwaukee (1-15).

    Portland (10-5) bounced back after dropping consecutive games to the Minnesota Timberwolves.

    In a recent development, lillard once again received a warm welcome from Bucks fans. Milwaukee ultimately waived him to sign center Myles Turner in the summer of 2025. The Bucks are still paying Lillard after they decided to stretch the remaining $113 million on his contract.

    So, on Thursday, Milwaukee fans watched their team lose its 12th straight game and Lillard shoot 10 of 18 from the field, including 5 of 12 from the beyond the arc.

    Plus, another former Bucks player, Jrue Holiday — part of Milwaukee's NBA championship team in 2020-21 — put on a show of his own. He logged 22 points, 7 assists and 4 steals.

    Holiday stepped back to hit a crucial jumper with about 5 ½ minutes to go. Another 36-year-old guard, Holiday went on to help the Trail Blazers create separation late, even coupling a steal with a layup.

    Portland also got 27 points and seven rebounds from a much younger member of its backcourt: Scoot Henderson.

    Meanwhile, the Bucks fell again, a day removed from facing Giannis Antetokounmpo for the first time.

    Recent findings suggest that milwaukee had four players score 15-plus points this time out. Tyler Herro led the way with 19, Kasparas Jakučionis and Nate Ament had 18 apiece and Ryan Rollins chipped in 15. Turner, notably, was out with a shoulder injury.

    Sources indicate that the lead changed hands incessantly on Thursday. Herro drew the Bucks within one at the 3:18 mark in the fourth quarter. The Trail Blazers, though, scored the final nine points, with Lillard netting the last two at the free-throw line.

    #4033. Commerce approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies, Rep. Mast says

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1206 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Commerce approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies, Rep. Mast says

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1206 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The subagency of the Commerce Department that regulates and enforces exports approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies including Alibaba and Tencent as of May 2026, according to documents released Thursday by the House Foreign Affairs Committee.
    • Industry observers note that some of those approvals, made by Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security, included sales to companies designated by the Department of Defense as "Chinese Military Companies," according to the documents.
    • "Over the past month, the administration's handling of chip export controls has put our national security and technology edge at risk.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The subagency of the Commerce Department that regulates and enforces exports approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies including Alibaba and Tencent as of May 2026, according to documents released Thursday by the House Foreign Affairs Committee.

    Industry observers note that some of those approvals, made by Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security, included sales to companies designated by the Department of Defense as "Chinese Military Companies," according to the documents. From December through May, companies had made 3.4 million requests for sales of U.S. AI chips to China, the committee reported, citing those made by Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices.

    "Over the past month, the administration's handling of chip export controls has put our national security and technology edge at risk. The Bureau of Industry and Security has failed to enforce the rules, and Congress must now conduct rigorous oversight of the administration's policies," Rep. Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, mentioned at a meeting of the panel Thursday at which members voted to release the documents.

    Recent findings suggest that spokespersons for Nvidia and AMD mentioned their companies comply with U.S. export control laws.

    Nvidia argued it was following the Commerce Department regulations that were in effect at the time.

    It has been revealed that A spokesperson from the Bureau of Industry and Security remarked it shared information with Congress on both approvals and denials of licenses for Nvidia's H200 and comparable chips. "Licensing decisions are the product of deliberation and consultation among multiple U.S. Government agencies," the spokesperson said.

    In a recent development, "The review and licensing process spanned more than half a year, with approvals subject to strict conditions and limited volumes. Despite receiving some licenses, we have since stopped shipping H200s to China," Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo told CNBC.

    On Tuesday, Nvidia reported $2.4 billion in quarterly revenue from H200 and related chip sales in China. In total, customers based in China and Hong Kong made up about 9.5% of all revenue.

    Industry observers note that "AMD complies with applicable U.S. export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations," AMD noted through a spokesperson.

    The approval of 879,000 AI chips is "not that many," Bernstein Senior Analyst Stacy Rasgon told CNBC, adding that this news is not surprising.

    Sources indicate that "It doesn't sound to me like they're approving everything they got willy nilly," Rasgon said of the Commerce Department. With 879,000 approvals out of 3.4 million requested AI chip sales, he added, "There was a process in place, and it sounds like they approved about one out of every four.".

    In a recent development, despite a rapid succession of China export controls on AI chips that started under the Biden administration in 2022, Nvidia and AMD both re-engineered some chips to comply and be sold legally in China. And in December, Trump remarked Nvidia could ship H200s, its older generation Hopper chips, to "approved customers in China" if the U.S. got a 25% cut of sales.

    The U.S. then licensed Nvidia H200 sales to Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance and other Chinese companies, although sales were limited because Beijing didn't approve large-scale imports, chip analyst Patrick Moorhead of Moor Insights & Strategy told CNBC last week.

    H200 sales numbers remained low due to those restrictions on China's end. Nvidia stated H200 shipments to China made up less than 1% of data center revenue for the quarter that ended in July.

    "In the grand context of the size of this market and how much they're shipping, it's a rounding error. It's tiny," Rasgon told CNBC.

    It has been revealed that the committee cited the Export Control Reform Act as justification for releasing the data. The panel said the law allows it to declassify and release export data if it "determines that the withholding of the following information is contrary to the national interest.".

    The license requests released by the Foreign Affairs Committee include requests to sell to major firms including ByteDance, Tesla (Shanghai) and Baidu.

    The release of documents comes in the wake of Jensen Huang's resignation from the chip supplier Nvidia after news surfaced that he had several extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy that led to concerns about Nvidia chips being diverted to China.

    In the weeks since, Republicans and Democrats in Congress have called for legislation to be passed that would impose stricter export controls on the sale of advanced AI chips to China and other adversaries.

    Industry observers note that "The license information we are disclosing today will help inform the American public about how BIS has handled licenses for Nvidia H200 and equivalent AMD chips to China. The public has the right to know how these decisions were made," Meeks mentioned.

    Mast mentioned two of the firms listed in Nvidia license applications to BIS — Maginfra and New Matrix — are suspected "smuggling fronts." The New York Times reported in November that both companies had empty offices and had ties to companies under national security sanctions.

    "Both are fake companies. If BIS approved the sale of these chips to these firms, obviously that is of tremendous concern to us — especially given that President Trump made clear last year that the sale of any AI chips to China will have very real national security conditions," Mast said at the Thursday meeting.

    Maginfra and Latest Matrix did not reply to requests for comment.

    Shares of AMD fell Thursday after the investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging the company "has its own China problem." The report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the company kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers.".

    CNBC did not independently verify this information.

    Fallout from the Huang scandal on Capitol Hill has intensified in the last week, as lawmakers question the degree to which the former head of Nvidia's relationship with the suspected Chinese spy could have jeopardized national security and American AI dominance.

    Huang is due for a closed-door transcribed interview with the House Foreign Affairs panel and two other committees on Dec. 1. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter is scheduled to appear before the panels Dec. 2.

    Senate banking committee Chair Tim Scott, R-S.C., declared on CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Wednesday that Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had also agreed to testify.

    Sources indicate that lutnick has come under fire over his relationship to Huang and for his failure to take action on Megaspeed, the Singaporean company where Alice Huang, with whom the former Nvidia CEO had an affair, was an executive until 2025. U.S. investigators suspect Megaspeed diverted Nvidia chips to China.

    Amid that criticism, the Commerce Department on Monday issued an interim final rule to close a loophole that has allowed Chinese companies to lease Nvidia's advancing computing power from data centers in third countries.

    The rule was "written by and at the direction of" the Treasury Department and the White House National Security Council, BIS mentioned in a press release.

    — Megan Cassella, Daren Fonda and Kif Leswing contributed to this report.

    The Tech Download: Anthropic charmed Wall Street. But one substantial uncertainty hangs over the business

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (704 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Anthropic's historic debut on Thursday saw the organization defy a wider tech selloff, as investors paid a premium for the stock.
    • The five-year-old tech giant, which raised $81.3 billion as part of the listing, is one of the first opportunities for public markets to value a pure play AI lab.
    • Many see the IPO as a possible savior of the AI trade after a shaky few months, but one big uncertainty hangs over the company's future prospects.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Anthropic's historic debut on Thursday saw the organization defy a wider tech selloff, as investors paid a premium for the stock.

    The five-year-old tech giant, which raised $81.3 billion as part of the listing, is one of the first opportunities for public markets to value a pure play AI lab.

    Many see the IPO as a possible savior of the AI trade after a shaky few months, but one big uncertainty hangs over the company's future prospects.

    "One of Anthropic's biggest challenges will be securing enough compute to support their steep growth trajectory," Gil Luria, D.A. Davidson, head of technology research, told me.

    Access to the huge quantities of compute the company needs to continue developing and deploying models is a massive challenge for Anthropic, which didn't respond to a request for comment for this piece, to navigate. It also comes at a time when there's growing public opposition to major data centers and delays to some AI infrastructure projects.

    Anthropic has remarked it has entered into purchase commitments and lease agreements for compute and infrastructure worth around $900 billion. The firm expects to incur roughly half of that cost before the end of 2030, with the rest between 2031 and 2045. Around $186 billion of that spend is tied to deals that can be terminated or subject to conditions like securing financing, facilities or regulatory approvals.

    There have been signs of hurdles for access to some of that capacity.

    Industry observers note that lambda missed a deadline to secure a facility lease for a $34.9 billion agreement, Anthropic noted in a filing earlier this month. Nscale disclosed that it had yet to secure binding financing commitments for its Anthropic contracts, which are worth up to around $44 billion. Lambda didn't respond to a request for comment and Nscale declined to comment.

    According to recent reports, "In both cases the financing risk falls on the neoclouds and their lenders, not on Anthropic," Nick Patience, AI lead at Futurum Group, told me. But, he added, the "real question is whether that capacity arrives on time.".

    It has been revealed that anthropic has cloud infrastructure commitments with Amazon and Google worth more than $100 billion each extending into the 2030s. It also could end up spending more than $100 billion with SpaceX to access AI compute.

    So, no shortage of major-money deals for graphics processing units, or GPUs, access.

    But even if some of the smaller deals collapse or take longer to get off the ground than expected, it could slow Anthropic down.

    "Demand is running ahead of supply, so missing capacity turns into lost revenue very quickly," stated Patience.

    Margins could suffer too, he added, as a result of increased costs of short-term compute commitments.

    Anthropic has said that long-term capacity is significantly cheaper than short-term commitments, which it would need to turn to when "customer demand or research needs exceed this long-term capacity.".

    Capacity constraints will be a challenge Anthropic has to navigate.

    "Throughout 2027-2028 we are expecting the firm to remain compute constrained, using a mixture of short-term compute to augment longer-term deals with the hyperscalers coming online," Malik Ahmed Khan, senior equity analyst at Morningstar, told me.

    Some slippage in terms of AI infrastructure delivery is likely, said Patience, but a "serious shortage is not, because its biggest suppliers are also its biggest investors and have every reason to keep it supplied.".

    Google and Amazon both have stakes in Anthropic that are worth well over $100 billion each. That's some incentive to deliver.

    Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress faces a divided workforce as some employees push for Jensen Huang's return.

    China's military seeks Nvidia's advanced chips for AI capabilities, commission indicates.

    Zelenskyy claims Starshield speed curbs still in place over parts of Ukraine.

    Widespread outages hit banks, air travel, the NSA and Apple, disrupting seemingly everything.

    'Standing on one leg': IMF chief warns about global economy as AI circular financing hits $1 trillion.

    Anthropic employees are set to experience a windfall from the company's IPO.

    The average Anthropic employee could be worth over $40 million after the organization's IPO on Thursday, with over 400 employees likely to be worth over $100 million, according to SEC filings and investors.

    #4012. Breaking: Is a bottom in for the Nasdaq-100? Charts to watch

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (583 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Is a bottom in for the Nasdaq-100? Charts to watch

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (583 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).
    • Sources indicate that is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in?
    • First, let's remember how we got here.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).

    Sources indicate that is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in? We're going to look at several charts to help answer that question.

    First, let's remember how we got here. In September, the NDX broke out from a bullish cup-and-handle pattern, producing a 33,200-upside target. That breakout rapidly failed, however, and gave way to a bearish pattern that broke down aggressively two weeks ago.

    The decline brought the index relatively close to its 26,350 downside target before the current rebound began.

    In a recent development, zooming out, it's telling to see where the bounce originated. Three crucial forms of support converged in the 25,000-26,000 area:.

    This confluence of support helped encourage buying after a roughly 15% decline.

    For perspective, we also see what larger drawdowns of 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% would look like … a lot worse.

    According to recent reports, the following chart tracks NDX drawdowns from 52-week highs going back to just after the financial crisis. Only a handful of declines exceeded 20%, and three produced relatively quick reversals: late 2018, the Covid lows in 2020 and April 2025.

    Historically, buying into declines of approximately 15%–25% has generally paid off, even when additional downside occurred first (yellow highlights).

    The chart also highlights previous declines of 10%–16% in green, putting the current pullback into perspective.

    The major exception was 2022, when the NDX eventually declined nearly 36% over approximately 10 months ... a much worse outcome, which many investors are concerned could happen again now.

    That raises the key question: Are we experiencing another routine correction, or the early stages of a larger bear market?

    One notable clue will be how far this bounce progresses.

    Sources indicate that any rally that fails to reclaim the previous highs could establish a significant lower high. Additional lower highs would provide stronger evidence of a developing, longer downtrend.

    We saw this in March 2022, when that first sharp rebound effort failed to reach the previous high before a much more severe decline followed.

    The bottom line: The current bounce is encouraging, particularly given where it originated and knowing how well buying prior 10-20% drawdowns has paid off.

    Industry observers note that from here, it's all about the follow through. We don't need to see new highs right away, but any rally from here that's met with another wave of strong selling could reignite downside momentum.

    #4007. Breaking: A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (625 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (625 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct.
    • However, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive.
    • Buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct. 6. The market despises uncertainty, and losing a visionary founder, particularly one without a well-telegraphed succession plan, makes it worse.

    However, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive. Trading in the $160s, Nvidia's valuation has taken a significant haircut, yet its underlying business fundamentals remain largely intact. While Huang was the architect of Nvidia's AI dominance, the manufacturer's moat — superior GPUs, the CUDA software ecosystem, and networking expertise — does not walk out the door with him. The company's structural advantage in the global artificial intelligence rollout persists.

    Buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options. Huang's departure guarantees that Nvidia will be operating under a cloud of transition for the foreseeable future. Executing a permanent CEO search while navigating global regulatory scrutiny takes time. Consequently, Nvidia's implied volatility (IV)—the market's pricing of expected future price swings — has spiked to highs not seen since the tariff tantrum in the first half of 2025, and this elevated IV is highly likely to persist for several months as the leadership drama slowly unfolds.

    It has been revealed that this prolonged period of high implied volatility can be a goldmine for option sellers, specifically those executing options overlays such as covered call strategies. When you buy NVDA shares at these depressed levels and simultaneously sell out-of-the-money call options against your position, the premiums you collect are directly tied to IV. Because fear and transition-related uncertainty have dramatically inflated these option prices, the income generated from selling covered calls is now significantly higher than usual.

    This lowers the risk profile of holding the stock considerably over time. Consistently collecting these inflated premiums systematically lowers your overall cost basis in the underlying shares. If the stock trades sideways or recovers slowly during the CEO search, you are generating an outsized cash yield on a stagnant asset. If the stock experiences further downside turbulence, the heavy premium income acts as a substantial downside buffer, meaningfully reducing the strategy's overall risk over time.

    By deploying a persistent covered call strategy, investors can leverage the exact fear driving the stock down to generate robust, risk-reducing income while maintaining exposure to the undeniable future of AI.

    #4004. Senate passes BAAJA permitting reform bill backed by AI, energy sectors

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1076 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Senate passes BAAJA permitting reform bill backed by AI, energy sectors

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1076 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Senate on Thursday passed a long-sought bill to ease the nation's environmental permitting laws and overhaul electrical transmission regulations, a crucial step toward boosting construction for the energy and technology industries.
    • Senators voted 62-33 to pass the bill, which split Democrats just weeks after they flipped enough seats from Republicans in the midterm elections to give them majorities in both chambers of Congress in January.
    • The vote offers a window into the fissures forming in the Democratic Party as it prepares to assume full control of Congress in January and tries to address the affordability crisis that catapulted it to power.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Senate on Thursday passed a long-sought bill to ease the nation's environmental permitting laws and overhaul electrical transmission regulations, a crucial step toward boosting construction for the energy and technology industries.

    Senators voted 62-33 to pass the bill, which split Democrats just weeks after they flipped enough seats from Republicans in the midterm elections to give them majorities in both chambers of Congress in January. The bill, known as the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, is projected to lower energy costs for consumers while weakening some environmental laws to speed up the permitting process.

    The vote offers a window into the fissures forming in the Democratic Party as it prepares to assume full control of Congress in January and tries to address the affordability crisis that catapulted it to power.

    More Democrats voted against the permitting measure than voted for it. Still, more than a dozen — including Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y. — voted to pass it over the objections of climate groups and tribes to get the bill across the finish line.

    "It's going to be legislation that's really going to make the biggest difference for the next 100 years, especially bringing down carbon emissions once this president is gone," Sen. Ruben Gallego, D-Ariz., told reporters on Thursday before the vote. Gallego supported the measure.

    The bill's Senate passage is a key step to it becoming law, but it would also need to clear the House before heading to President Donald Trump's desk.

    In a recent development, democratic supporters of the bill touted its cost benefits as a win after they ran campaigns on affordability, and pointed to a massive glut of clean energy the bill could bring onto the grid. Opponents lamented rollbacks to the nation's bedrock environmental protection laws favored by the fossil fuel industry and Republicans, and warned the measure could offer carte blanche authority to the data centers undergirding artificial intelligence.

    According to recent reports, "No big, bipartisan bill is going to be perfect for everyone, but we have a real opportunity to make electricity more affordable for families. Working people can't afford to wait another few years for us to get this done," Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M., the incoming chair of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee and an author of the bill, stated in a statement to CNBC.

    Heinrich brokered the agreement with his counterpart Sen. Mike Lee, R-Utah, along with Sens. Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I., and Shelley Moore Capito, R-W.Va., the top Democrat and Republican on the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee.

    "Earlier this month, Americans sent a clear message: They want Congress focused on making their lives more affordable. That's precisely what this permitting reform bill will do," he stated.

    It has been revealed that getting to a final vote was acrimonious. Senators amended the package in the weeks leading up to the vote to address concerns from Native American tribes, which objected to changes in their participation in permitting.

    "I'm not going to sit around and let these data centers scar our treasures," Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore., told reporters Thursday about the push for his amendment, which would have blocked data centers from being built on public lands.

    Clean energy and fossil energy groups both cheered the bill's passage in the Senate.

    As negotiated, the bill would benefit both renewables and fossil fuels. Artificial intelligence and the broader tech industry also stand to benefit — despite the bill's provision forcing hyperscalers to pay for upgrades to the grid — as power-hungry data centers demand more electricity.

    The American Clean Power Association, a group that represents renewables, mentioned it was "a clean energy bill that will modernize America's energy systems and lower consumer prices.".

    The American Petroleum Institute, which represents the oil and gas industry, called the bill a "major breakthrough on historic permitting reforms that would deliver more affordable energy for consumers, cut costly delays, and build much-needed critical infrastructure.".

    Renewables would benefit largely from the bill's electricity transmission component, along with measures aimed at blocking Trump from cancelling already-permitted wind and solar projects. New solar and wind projects are often bottlenecked by a lack of transmission able to deliver power to the grid.

    Rhodium Group, an economic research firm, estimates the bill would allow an additional 17 to 249 gigawatts of clean energy to be built by 2040. Natural gas exports would rise 8% to 15% beyond a 76% to 145% rise already accounted for under current policy. Greenhouse gases would be reduced by 5 to 148 million metric tons annually in 2040.

    Sources indicate that "A lot of Democrats are involved and supportive in this deal because expanding grid capacity would integrate a lot of clean energy," stated Rob Gramlich, the founder and president of Grid Strategies, an energy consulting group. "Republicans are maybe less interested in that benefit, but they do care about economic growth and serving new large loads. And I think members on both sides of the aisle are pretty well aware that we're doing much less grid investment here in the U.S. compared to other countries.".

    Gramlich added that "you can't get to 60 to 80% of our grid from renewable energy without a significant expansion of grid capacity.".

    However, the Natural Resources Defense Council was among the opponents.

    "The House should not pass a bill that gives President Trump a blank check to reward oil and gas companies and data center developers," the organization stated in a statement. "Lawmakers should oppose this bill and try again next year to pass legislation worthy of the American people, not for the fossil fuel industry and data center companies.".

    The bill now heads to the House, where Republican leadership is expected to attempt to pass it. Trump also supports the deal.

    But as in the Senate, Democrats are expected to be divided.

    "Democrats promised to lower bills, cut pollution, and protect ratepayers," mentioned Rep. Scott Peters, D-Calif., a longtime champion of permitting reform. "Voters are giving us a chance to show we mean it. BAAJA does all three. We should pass it before the end of this Congress.".

    House Natural Resources ranking member and likely incoming Chair Jared Huffman, D-Calif., meanwhile, urged Democrats to say no to the permitting bill.

    "Don't believe the lie that this terrible bill, exactly as drafted, is the last, best and only chance to ever do permitting reform," he said. "We can produce a better deal.".

    AI can help find holiday deals — but it's not great at spotting scams, experts say

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (514 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Artificial intelligence shopping tools can help consumers compare prices and find gift ideas, but experts say shoppers still need to verify unfamiliar retailers and sellers before buying.
    • According to recent reports, scammers can use AI to make fake stores, product photos and reviews look convincing.
    • According to recent reports, "The biggest impact right now we're seeing in AI is on coding," Bilge said.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Artificial intelligence shopping tools can help consumers compare prices and find gift ideas, but experts say shoppers still need to verify unfamiliar retailers and sellers before buying.

    According to recent reports, scammers can use AI to make fake stores, product photos and reviews look convincing. It can also make creating and deploying websites easier, mentioned Leyla Bilge, global head of scam research at cybersecurity company Norton.

    According to recent reports, "The biggest impact right now we're seeing in AI is on coding," Bilge said. Scammers can register "thousands and thousands of fake e-shops online," she said, which increases the chances shoppers will encounter one.

    A Norton survey of 1,000 U.S. adults found that 16% of respondents had been scammed while shopping online during the holidays. Of those victims, 88% lost money, with an average loss of $394. The survey was conducted from an opt-in online panel between Sept. 10 and 21 by Dynata on behalf of Norton's parent firm, Gen.

    Here's a look at more stories on how to manage, grow and protect your money for the years ahead.

    Scams can have impacts beyond financial losses. In a survey of 3,110 U.S. adults released in June, the Global Anti-Scam Alliance found that 82% of respondents had encountered a scam in the past year. More than half, 59%, said the scam affected their mental well-being.

    More than half of GASA survey respondents remarked they had experienced repeat scams.

    If you put your address or phone number in an AI tool that turns out to be fraudulent, "you might get reached out to again with a much more sophisticated, much more targeted and personalized attack and scam," Bilge said.

    Among respondents who had used an AI shopping assistant or agent, 56% mentioned it had recommended or completed a purchase from a retailer they didn't recognize, the Norton survey found.

    An agent focused on finding the lowest price may steer a shopper toward an unfamiliar seller, so experts say shoppers shouldn't treat its recommendation as vetted.

    "You absolutely need to check with the retailer directly," mentioned Matt Schulz, chief consumer finance analyst at LendingTree and author of "Ask Questions, Save Money, Make More.".

    According to recent reports, bilge said many shoppers make purchases on their phones through social media, sometimes with a single click, leaving them little time or incentive to assess where the link goes. Then, some still buy even if they're unsure of the site's legitimacy.

    The Norton survey also found that 35% of Americans had bought from a website or seller they thought might be a scam because the deal seemed too good to pass up.

    Before buying from a seller or retailer, consumer experts recommend these steps:.

    While AI can narrow gift options and find the lowest prices, experts say shoppers should verify the store before handing over payment details — and, when possible, pay by credit card. Keep order details and receipts, too.

    The FTC indicates cardholders can dispute charges in certain cases, such as when merchandise never arrives.

    — CNBC's Stephanie Dhue contributed reporting to this article.

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (401 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Intuit to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (401 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tax software maker Intuit said Thursday that it has agreed to sell marketing subsidiary Mailchimp to Italian technology consolidator Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion in cash and stock.
    • Industry observers note that the sale is a costly retreat for Intuit, which paid $12 billion for Mailchimp in 2021 in a push beyond its core tax and accounting businesses.
    • The deal is the latest instance of Bending Spoons picking up a once promising technology asset.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tax software maker Intuit said Thursday that it has agreed to sell marketing subsidiary Mailchimp to Italian technology consolidator Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion in cash and stock. The deal is set to close in early 2027, according to a statement.

    Industry observers note that the sale is a costly retreat for Intuit, which paid $12 billion for Mailchimp in 2021 in a push beyond its core tax and accounting businesses. Five years later, the software maker is unloading the email-marketing company for less than one-third of that price after Mailchimp became a drag on its overall revenue growth.

    The deal is the latest instance of Bending Spoons picking up a once promising technology asset. The organization bought productivity software startup Airtable in September for 10% of what it was once worth.

    The Bending Spoons portfolio also contains AOL, Brightcove, Eventbrite, Evernote, Meetup, Vimeo, and WeTransfer.

    In August Intuit started running Mailchimp as a distinct operating segment. The move was meant to give investors more transparency as the company tried to manage the unit for profitability, Sandeep Aujla, Intuit's finance chief, stated at a September company briefing.

    Also on Thursday, Intuit revealed stronger-than-expected earnings and revenue for its fiscal first quarter, which ended on Oct. 31. The organization reported $2.91 in adjusted earnings per share on $4.35 billion in revenue. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for $2.70 per share and $4.31 billion in revenue.

    While Intuit's revenue increased 12% year over year, Mailchimp revenue declined 1% to $313 million. Analysts polled by StreetAccount had expected $314.4 million.

    According to recent reports, management called for $22.88 to $23.12 in adjusted earnings per share for the 2027 fiscal year, with $23.081 billion to $23.365 billion in revenue. Analysts polled by LSEG had predicted $23.62 in adjusted earnings per share on $23.43 billion in revenue. Intuit shares tumbled 15% in extended trading.

    Sources indicate that the organization said Mailchimp should produce $1.256 billion to $1.266 billion in fiscal 2027 revenue, which would be down 1% to flat year over year. In August Aujla said Intuit anticipated Mailchimp's higher effective prices offsetting increased client churn. Mailchimp was founded in 2001. Rivals include Klaviyo, which went public in 2023.

    Berkshire Hathaway invested $600 million in Bending Spoons when the acquirer went public in July, and in October Bending Spoons stated Berkshire invested another $330 million.

    #3991. Berkshire breaks out to record high with fourth-quarter rally reaching 19%

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Berkshire breaks out to record high with fourth-quarter rally reaching 19%

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1116 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.
    • Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.
    • The much more widely held B shares closed at newly introduced highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.

    Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.

    The much more widely held B shares closed at newly introduced highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.

    The gains are in sharp contrast to the S&P 500's 1.2% dip as investors appear to be seeing Berkshire as a relatively safe haven amid worries about AI stocks and spending.

    Both Berkshire classes were up 3.9% on the week as the S&P advanced by 2.5%, its best week since early August.

    Berkshire's B shares are now 7.5 percentage points ahead of the benchmark for the year so far.

    After erasing their post-Buffett CEO announcement losses three weeks ago, Berkshire shares are now up almost 10% since last year's shareholders meeting.

    They've gained around 29% since last August's lows and are up around 18% year-to-date.

    Berkshire Hathaway is due to disclose its quarterly equity portfolio snapshot on Monday when it files its Q3 13F with the SEC.

    We won't know for sure until then, but numbers in the organization's third quarter 10-Q, released last Saturday, indicate Berkshire continued to reduce its Bank of America stake.

    It would be the ninth consecutive quarter of selling.

    As of June 30, Berkshire reported holding 483.4 million BAC shares valued now at $24.7 billion, it's fifth largest equity position.

    On June 30, 2024, before the selling began, Berkshire owned just over 1 billion shares valued at $41.1 billion.

    Since then, the number of shares in the portfolio has decreased by 53.2%, not including any Q3 sales, while the stock price has increased by 28.3%.

    If there had been no reductions, the position would be worth $52.7 billion.

    The belief Berkshire sold more BAC shares in the third quarter is based on a $372 million reduction in the cost basis for equities categorized by the firm as "banks, insurance, and finance.".

    The 10-Q also reports $2.2 billion of pretax gains from equity sales.

    Industry observers note that barron's notes Bank of America and American Express are the only financial stocks in the portfolio that have a cost basis low enough to generate a gain like that. Amex is one of the four stocks new CEO Greg Abel indicated would be held for "decades" to come in his February letter to shareholders.

    In any case, Berkshire's almost 23% stake in Amex would have required it to quickly disclose any sales.

    Based on the numbers in the 10-Q, the warrants Berkshire received as part of a 2011 $5 billion investment in the bank that it used in 2017 to buy 700 million shares at $7.14 each, and BAC's average stock price in the quarter, Barron's estimates 30 to 40 million shares may have been sold.

    That would be roughly in line with the 30.2 million shares sold in the second quarter.

    The case isn't as good, but Barron's thinks Berkshire may have bought more Alphabet shares in the period. That's based on a $2.3 billion increase in the cost basis for the category that includes Google's parent.

    Overall, it looks like it will be a relatively quiet quarter with $2.4 billion in equity purchases and $2.8 billion in sales.

    Recent findings suggest that in the first quarter, Berkshire bought $15.9 billion and sold $24.1 billion of equities. In the second quarter, it purchased $23.5 billion and sold $3.7 billion.

    All those numbers exclude the tech giant's buybacks of its own stock.

    In a term sheet filed early Friday, Berkshire Hathaway says it is selling more than 182 billion yen ($1.1 billion) worth of bonds with maturities between 2029 and 2056 and annual interest rates between 2.6% and 4.6%.

    Bloomberg points out the rates, compared to benchmarks, are higher than its previous sale this year.

    It quotes a fund manager as saying market sentiment "has become more sensitive," forcing issuers to make their offerings more attractive.

    In April, Berkshire sold 272 billion yen ($1.7 billion) of bonds.

    Berkshire uses the proceeds from the yen-denominated bonds to protect its ongoing investments in Japanese stocks from currency fluctuations.

    Some links may require a subscription:.

    Warren Buffett recommends Benjamin Graham's book, "The Intelligent Investor," and outlines what he considers Graham's three most important ideas.

    Industry observers note that WARREN BUFFETT: On investment books, if you're asking about that, I would recommend the first two books that Phil Fisher wrote back around 1960, "Common Sense [Stocks] and Uncommon Profits" and the second one ["Paths to Wealth Through Common Stocks"]. They're very good books.

    You know, I obviously recommend, first and foremost, [Benjamin Graham's] "The Intelligent Investor," with chapters eight and 20 are the ones that you really should read.

    Sources indicate that two of the — well, all of the vital ideas in investing, really, are in that book, because there's only about three ideas. And those — two of them are emphasized in those two chapters...

    One is that — to think of yourself — to think of investing as owning a business and not buying something that wiggles around in price.

    Recent findings suggest that and the second one is your attitude, which ties in with that, the attitude toward the market, that's covered in chapter eight. And if you have the proper attitude toward market movements, it's an enormous help in securities.

    And the final chapter is on the margin of safety, which means, don't try and drive a 9,800-pound truck over a bridge that claims it's, you know, "Capacity: 10,000 pounds." But go down the road a little bit and find one that says, "Capacity: 15,000 pounds.".

    Berkshire market capitalization: $1,259,897,054,755.

    Berkshire Cash as of Sept 30: $377.4 billion (Up 3.3% from June 30).

    Excluding Rail Cash and Subtracting T-Bills Payable: $352.3 billion (Down 1.9% from June 30).

    Berkshire repurchased $9.6 billion of its shares in Q3 2026.

    Berkshire's top holdings of disclosed publicly traded stocks in the U.S. and Japan, by market value, based on the latest closing prices.

    The full list of holdings and current market values is available from CNBC.com's Berkshire Hathaway Portfolio Tracker.

    Kushner notes Russia 'comfortable' with idea of NATO-like security guarantees for Ukraine

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (520 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • envoy Jared Kushner has stated Russia may accept NATO-like security guarantees for Ukraine, adding that President Donald Trump wants to bring an end to Russia's full-scale invasion "with Europe by his side.".
    • His comments come shortly after Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping held historic trilateral talks on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, a meeting that did not appear to result in any concessions on Ukraine or European security.
    • "I think we've got the Russians comfortable with that concept where any security guarantee for Ukraine would be based on Article 5," Kushner said alongside European leaders at a news conference in Germany on Thursday, referring to the part of NATO's treaty that enshrines the principle of collective defense.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that U.S. envoy Jared Kushner has stated Russia may accept NATO-like security guarantees for Ukraine, adding that President Donald Trump wants to bring an end to Russia's full-scale invasion "with Europe by his side.".

    His comments come shortly after Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping held historic trilateral talks on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, a meeting that did not appear to result in any concessions on Ukraine or European security.

    "I think we've got the Russians comfortable with that concept where any security guarantee for Ukraine would be based on Article 5," Kushner said alongside European leaders at a news conference in Germany on Thursday, referring to the part of NATO's treaty that enshrines the principle of collective defense.

    "I think that that comes with at least what the Russians are saying, which is their intention is, when this war is over, to not have another war in the future," he added. Kushner, who is Trump's son-in-law, was at the conference in Berlin alongside fellow U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff.

    They have led the Trump administration's efforts to end Russia's nearly five-year-long war with Ukraine.

    It has been revealed that article 5 defines an attack against one NATO member as an attack against all members. The alliance calls it a "unique and enduring principle that binds its members together, committing them to protect each other and setting a spirit of solidarity.".

    Industry observers note that ukraine has long held ambitions to join the alliance. Russia has previously mentioned that if Kyiv joined NATO, it would cause problems for many years.

    It was not immediately clear what form potential security guarantees would take, or whether Russia or Ukraine would accept them. Russia's Foreign Ministry, Ukraine's Foreign Ministry and NATO were not immediately available to comment when contacted by CNBC on Friday morning.

    "From America's perspective, giving an Article 5-like security guarantee is a really, really substantial deal and I think that that is something that President Trump is open to, but obviously it has to be in America's interest to do that," Kushner noted.

    Russia released a wave of missile and drone attacks on Ukraine's energy and transport infrastructure overnight, damaging three bridges in Kyiv and killing at least three people, authorities remarked.

    Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko stated via Telegram on Friday that Kyiv's Podilskyi, Darnytskyi and Southern crossings had been damaged by missile strikes, with experts currently assessing the damage.

    Russia's Defense Ministry noted it had carried out a "massive" strike on several Ukrainian cities, targeting enterprises of the country's defense industry and warehouses used in the production and storage of missiles and drones.

    Putin vowed on Thursday that Russia would respond to Ukraine's attacks on the Kerch Bridge, adding it would be "much more painful." The bridge, which links Russia to occupied Crimea and is one of Putin's signature projects, was damaged by repeated Ukrainian attacks this week.

    Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Tuesday described it as an "unprecedented operation" several weeks in the making, with Ukraine's defense forces, security services and weapons manufacturers involved.
